facts.statement: Fossils of Cedarosaurus were discovered in 1996 in eastern Utah within the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: The fossils were discovered in 1996 in eastern Utah within the rocks of the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus was officially named and described by Tidwell, Carpenter, and Brooks in 1999.
facts.quote: It was officially named and described by Tidwell, Carpenter and Brooks in 1999.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Cedarosaurus could reach a maximum length of 15 meters and a mass of 10 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the maximum length up to 15 m and mass up to 10 MT.

facts.statement: A 2001 study analyzed 115 gastroliths found associated with a Cedarosaurus specimen.
facts.quote: In 2001 Frank Sanders, Kim Manley, and Kenneth Carpenter published a study on 115 gastroliths discovered in association with a Cedarosaurus specimen.

facts.statement: The total mass of the gastroliths found with the Cedarosaurus specimen was 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: The total mass of the gastroliths themselves was 7 kg.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the high surface area of the largest gastroliths indicates they may have helped grind or crush ingested plant material.
facts.quote: The high surface area to volume ratio of the largest clasts suggests that the gastroliths may have broken down ingested plant material by grinding or crushing it.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus was a small-sized sauropod, reaching only 14 meters in length.
facts.quote: Cedarosaurus es un saurópodo de pequeño tamaño, solo tenía 14 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus possessed the typical nasal crest of brachiosaurids and had long front legs compared to its hind legs.
facts.quote: Poseía el típico arco nasal de los braquiosáuridos y largas patas delanteras comparadas con las traseras.

facts.statement: The average humerus of Cedarosaurus measured 1380 millimeters and the femur 1395 millimeters.
facts.quote: Su húmero media 1380 milímetros y el fémur 1395.

facts.statement: The ratio of the radius's minimum circumference to its length is 0.31 in Cedarosaurus.
facts.quote: La relación de la circunferencia mínima del radio a su longitud es 0,31 en Cedarosaurus.

facts.statement: The neural spines of the middle tail vertebrae in Cedarosaurus slant forward when the vertebrae are aligned.
facts.quote: Las apófisis neurales de las vértebras de la cola media se inclinan hacia delante cuando las vértebras están alineadas.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus fossils come from the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Formation in western Utah and the Paluxy Formation in Texas, USA.
facts.quote: Los restos del Cedarosaurus provienen del miembro Yellow Cat de la Formación Cedar, en el oeste de Utah, y de la Formación Paluxy, Texas, en los Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The genus name Cedarosaurus refers to the discovery location, while the species name honors Carol Weiskopf.
facts.quote: El nombre de género viene dado por el lugar del hallazgo y la especie en honor a Carol Weiskopf.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus belongs to the family Brachiosauridae, which is distinctive for having femur and humerus bones of nearly the same size.
facts.quote: Cedarosaurus, pertenece a la familia Brachiosauridae, distintiva por los huesos fémur y húmero de casi el mismo tamaño.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus is classified as a brachiosaurid.
facts.quote: Cedarosaurus es un braquiosáurido.

facts.statement: In 2001, researchers published a study on 115 gastroliths found associated with a Cedarosaurus specimen.
facts.quote: En 2001, Frank Sanders , Kim Manley y Kenneth Carpenter publicaron un estudio sobre 115 gastrolitos descubiertos en asociación con un espécimen de Cedarosaurus.

facts.statement: The total mass of the gastroliths was 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: La masa total de los gastrolitos en sí era de 7 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The lightest stone weighed 0.1 gram, while most weighed 715 grams.
facts.quote: La piedra menos masiva peso 0,1 gramo y la mayoría 715 gramos

facts.statement: The gastroliths were composed mainly of chert, with some sandstone, limolite, and quartz grains also included.
facts.quote: Los gastrolitos estaban compuestos principalmente de sílex, Con un poco de piedra arenisca, limolita, y granos de cuarcita también se incluidos.

facts.statement: The high surface-area-to-volume ratio of the larger clasts suggests the gastroliths may have broken down ingested plant material by grinding or crushing it.
facts.quote: La alta relación área superficial sobre volumen de los clastos más grandes sugiere que los gastrolitos pueden haber descompuesto el material vegetal ingerido al molerlo o triturarlo.

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus belongs to the parent group Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachiosauridae

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus is classified in the family Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Brachiosauridae

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Cedarosaurus is Cedarosaurus weiskopfae.
facts.quote: Type species: Cedarosaurus weiskopfae

facts.statement: Cedarosaurus lived from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, between 137.05 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 110.1 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Cedarosaurus (meaning "Cedar lizard" - named after the Cedar Mountain Formation, in which it was discovered) is a genus of nasal-crested macronarian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period (Valanginian).
